extension.summary: tofa media server: user interface, plus a browsable video source
extension.description:
An unofficial client for the tofa media server (tofa.tv), in two parts.
Under Programs, tofa opens a full user interface: Home, Browse, Discover, Search, title detail with cast and episodes, its own player chrome, and Settings.
Under Video add-ons, the same library appears as a browsable source, so it can also be used in widgets, favourites and Kodi's own containers.
Both play through Kodi's native VideoPlayer, negotiating DirectPlay/DirectFile so Dolby Vision, TrueHD/DTS-HD passthrough and refresh-rate matching reach it untouched.
extension.disclaimer: An unofficial tofa client, engineered with the tofa team, who also help support it.
extension.news: - Needs tofa media server 0.12.0 or newer. An older server still works, but you are told once per session that some screens may be incomplete. - Mark a title Seen it or Not interested from its options menu: on Discover, on Suggested for You, and on a title you don't have. - Browse opens on Movies, TV Shows and Other, as tofa groups your libraries, instead of one tile per library. - A person's page lists their whole filmography at once, including the films in your library that they directed or wrote. - Show pages follow your profile's Missing episodes setting in tofa: Automatic, Always show or Never show. - Turning subtitles on skips commentary and short forced tracks when a full one is there, and the track list labels forced and commentary tracks.

extension.news: - The posters behind Browse's tiles drift at the Apple TV app's pace, and the picture dips briefly as you move between tiles, as on the Apple TV. - Watchlist can be sorted (Date Added, Title, Year, Rating, Runtime or Shuffle) and narrowed by genre or year. - Posters download much smaller where the server holds a large image, and the Videos library's backdrop shows many more different posters. - Fixed the title page's episode row moving focus onto a card that was mostly off the screen.

Both play through Kodi's native VideoPlayer, negotiating DirectPlay/DirectFile so Dolby Vision, TrueHD/DTS-HD passthrough and refresh-rate matching reach it untouched.

extension.news: - Household viewing: people in your household who have their own tofa account can now watch on this TV as themselves, with their own history, watchlist and Continue Watching. Turn it on under Settings > Account, on the account owner's own profile; Who's watching then lists them after your profiles. tofa asks who's watching each time it starts, and again after 15 minutes away. - When a household member's session ends, tofa goes back to Who's watching from whichever screen you are on. - Settings > Account is laid out as on the Apple TV app: This TV, then Account. Manage account shows the code to scan. - Collections can be sorted by name or by size. Sorted by name, an A-Z rail beside the film series shows just the ones under a letter. - Inside a collection, Unwatched and Filter now work: by watch status, format and year, wherever the collection's titles carry them. - History lists up to 100 titles, so a long run of one show's episodes no longer crowds everything else out. A title that has left your library shows once. - The A-Z rail is now the size of the Apple TV app's. - When the server cannot be reached at start, tofa now says so instead of showing empty screens. - Fixed a TV losing its tofa cloud sign-in, which made the Account page show a username instead of your email address. A TV that already lost it needs signing out and in again once. - Fixed Settings cutting off the last of four choices under a preview. - Fixed Collections drawing the film series heading over your second row of collections.

extension.summary: Fonts for the tofa for Kodi add-on
extension.description:
The typefaces the tofa for Kodi add-on draws its own screens in: Inter Tight, Roboto Mono and the Lucide icon set.
Installed automatically as a dependency of tofa for Kodi. It provides font files and nothing else: no screens, no settings, and nothing runs. It is not useful on its own.
Kodi looks inside enabled font resources for any font file it cannot find in the active skin, so tofa's screens can name these files without a copy of them being placed in the skin.
